narrative.overview: BioTracker is a durable, plainly-kept record of one person's own body data. The interface behaves like a well-made ledger: legible, ordered, honest about what it does and doesn't contain. Depth comes from structure — a fixed left rail, a centered reading column capped at 64rem, borders and tonal fills that separate without shouting — not from decoration. Teal is the one voice of the system; everything else is quiet ink on cool paper. The palette is a cool teal-slate on a barely-tinted near-white, with a single warm amber accent reserved for genuine attention. Type is one family (Aptos) across weights; there is no display face, because a ledger doesn't have a hero. The system rejects the consumer-wellness playbook — no gamification, no SaaS-cream, no gradient hero-metric, no wall-of-charts cockpit — and any visual cue that implies clinical authority.
keyCharacteristics: One accent voice (teal), amber reserved for genuine attention only
Flat-by-default: borders and tonal fills over shadows
Cool near-white paper, dark teal-slate ink, no warm-cream default
Single sans family (Aptos) across weights; no display face
Metric hues are for data series only, never for chrome
Honest presentation: -- for missing values, no dramatization

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only brand color on any given screen. Amber is an exception you must justify, not a second accent. If two colors are competing for attention, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Verdict Rule
rules.body: Color never renders a health judgment. A value is never tinted red for 'bad' or green for 'good'. The metric hues identify which series, not how the user is doing.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Aptos does every job. Never introduce a second typeface for 'personality' — hierarchy comes from weight and size, not from font pairing.

rules.name: The Honest Number Rule
rules.body: A missing metric renders as --, never as 0 and never hidden. The absence of data is itself information the ledger must show.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow is a statement of containment, not a style. If a shadow is doing decoration rather than grouping, delete it and use a border.

dos: Do keep teal as the one brand voice per screen; reserve amber for genuinely attention-worthy moments.
Do render missing metrics as --. Show gaps and flat trends honestly.
Do carry structure with 1px dividers and tonal fills; reserve shadow-soft for real containers.
Do use metric hues only to identify data series, in charts and series icons.
Do keep muted-foreground (#52677a) as the floor for secondary text — it holds 4.5:1 on paper.
Do pair numeric inputs with a unit chip so a value is never ambiguous.
Do use one family (Aptos) across weights for all hierarchy.
donts: Don't gamify: no streak badges, confetti, mascots, or dopamine loops.
Don't ship the generic SaaS-cream look — no warm cream background, gradient hero-metric, identical card grid, or tracked-uppercase eyebrow over every section.
Don't imply clinical authority: no red/green good-vs-bad tinting, no risk gauges, no diagnostic framing.
Don't build a data-overwhelming cockpit — one number per metric card, no wall of charts.
Don't add a second typeface for 'personality'.
Don't use shadow as decoration or let cards float; if a shadow isn't grouping content, use a border.
Don't use border-left/border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't use gradient text or background-clip: text anywhere.
